subject: Capacity reservation readout & ops checklist
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.r@deepinfer.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@deepinfer.com
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity reservation readout & ops checklist

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the team. Quick recap from our side and the key asks we want to make sure are captured: 

- Primary pain: unpredictable latency spikes during peak inference and noisy neighbors impacting throughput on multi-tenant endpoints. This is blocking our plans to move sensitive workloads (PHI) to production.
- Isolation need: single-tenant or otherwise strongly segmented pools (VPC/network isolation) for PHI workflows and audit separation.
- Throughput target: support sustained batch jobs (up to 400 qps aggregate) plus occasional spiky real-time traffic (~80 qps).
- Latency SLO: aiming for p99 < 250ms for 512-token contexts in normal operating windows.
- Cost/timeline: we have procurement and engineering alignment to commit in Q3 if the sizing + SLA fit. Procurement wants a clear ops acceptance plan and evidence (SOC2, runbooks).

Attached: deepinfer_cloud_requirements.xlsx (spec sheet) — includes expected qps, token distributions, and regulatory notes.

Next steps from us: confirm a sizing + ops plan and a window for performance validation.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Infrastructure
DeepInfer Inc.

Attachment: deepinfer_cloud_requirements.xlsx (xlsx, 34KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity reservation readout & ops checklist

Alex — thanks for the clear spec and for sharing the sheet. Short post-call recap and our recommended next actions (ops + commercial) so we have a common checklist: 

Confirmed pain & goals
- Latency spikes and noisy neighbor impact: agreed. We'll propose a single-tenant reserved pool to eliminate multi-tenant interference.
- Isolation & compliance: VPC + customer-managed ingress, audit logs, and key access controls are a priority for PHI.
- Throughput: we'll size for sustained 400 qps with headroom for bursts as you described.

Preliminary sizing recommendation (goal: balance cost vs performance)
- Option A (latency-first): 4x A100-class GPUs equivalent with reserved KV cache lanes for hot models — expected to meet p99 ~180–220ms for 512 tokens under target qps.
- Option B (cost-first): 8x A10-class equivalents (fractional throughput) with batching tuned; p99 expected ~230–300ms but lower unit cost.
- Isolation: single-tenant pool in your region (us-west) with network ACLs; private control plane option if you need on-prem routing later.

SLA & acceptance 
- Suggested SLA: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool with p99 latency target defined per model/context length.
- Acceptance tests: synthetic p99 benchmarks, 24h soak test at projected qps, and failover test to hosted fallback model variant.

Action items (owners)
- Ben: produce a formal sizing & ops checklist and attach the runbook/procurement docs (Ben to share by EOD).
- Alex: confirm procurement timeline & any legal constraints (PII/PHI clauses).
- Marissa: coordinate an ops benchmark week (two candidate weeks) and collect SOC2/network diagrams for review.

We can also propose an initial canary rollout (50% traffic to reserved pool, 50% to hosted) if you'd like staged validation.

Subject: Re: Capacity reservation readout & ops checklist

Alex / team — attaching a sizing proposal and an ops acceptance checklist for the reserved pool. Highlights and timeline below.

Attachment: reserved-pool-sizing-proposal.pdf (12 pages)

Ops highlights
- Bench plan:
  1) Synthetic latency/p99 run (three configs: baseline hosted, reserved Option A, reserved Option B)
  2) 24-hour soak at projected sustained qps (400) with token mix from your sheet
  3) Failover test to hosted fallback + cache-miss simulation
- Monitoring: token-level cost telemetry, per-model p99/p50, KV cache hit rate, and per-route tracing.
- Acceptance criteria (examples): p99 within target for two consecutive runs; no more than 2% request error rate during soak.
- Security artifacts we'll provide: SOC2 snapshot, network diagram, runbook excerpt, and audit log sample.

Operational timeline (proposed)
- Week 1 (Prep): exchange SOC2 + network details, finalize model binary & container versions. (Target: week of Jun 23)
- Week 2 (Bench): run the synthetic + soak tests (two candidate weeks below).
- Week 3 (Canary): staged production traffic ramp.

Candidate benchmark windows: Jul 7–11 or Jul 21–25. Please confirm which works for procurement and engineering.

Next commercial steps: once bench acceptance is complete, we can draft a reserved capacity commitment (monthly) and an ops SLA addendum.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
